# feat: route Anthropic subscriptions through Claude Code by ashx-j · Pull Request #107 · ashx-j/lunR

Anthropic subscription requests previously used direct OAuth over the Messages API. That bypasses the Claude Code subscription route. This PR sends subscription generations through Claude Code instead, while genuine Anthropic API keys keep their existing Messages API behavior. Legacy OAuth tokens now fail with setup instructions rather than falling back to direct HTTP.

The bridge reuses the pinned MIT Hermes Python transport for admission, replay, and process isolation. lunR still owns tools, permissions, and history. Python and Claude Code are checked only when someone explicitly chooses subscription login, and each missing-prerequisite installer requires a separate confirmation.

Offline validation: five package builds and the Node bundle; 36 focused AI tests, 19 focused coding-agent tests, 13 xAI compatibility tests, 20 vendored Python tests; first-paint and first-turn checks; vendor SHA verification; package dry run and relocated public-name worker import. Independent review caught an SDK routing failure and native cleanup gaps; both are fixed.

Live subscription qualification was **not** performed. I did not install Claude Code prerequisites or access an account. Synthetic native evals, cross-platform process checks, and a user-authorized subscription smoke remain release gates. No direct-OAuth fallback is enabled.

PR filed by GPT-6 Sol in the lunR agent.

# fix: send messages immediately during subagent waits by ashx-j · Pull Request #103 · ashx-j/lunR

When the parent was blocked inside `subagent_wait`, normal Enter still became a steering message. It sat under the editor until the wait ended, which made it impossible to redirect the parent while background agents were still working.

Now Enter releases only the active local wait, lets the current tool batch settle, and starts the text as a fresh parent prompt. Background children and sibling tools keep running. Alt+Enter follow-ups and ordinary steering outside `subagent_wait` are unchanged.

The handoff is scoped to the owning agent run, waits for full `agent_settled`, preserves images and input transforms, and keeps rapid submissions in FIFO order.

Remote sessions must preserve the real TUI and install without requiring users to compile a PTY library. This prerequisite PR tests that foundation. It does not implement remote hosting.

Work is paused. The agreed next milestone is Windows hosting through npm, manual host startup, and reconnecting to the same live task from another local terminal. Other host operating systems, standalone delivery, and broad service/VPN automation are deferred from that milestone.

[Full validation run 36053877314](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/actions/runs/36053877314) passed all 12 jobs at [5aa58d4](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/commit/5aa58d4210a7c5f2163d632653363dd24cc50839), with no diagnostic bypass: six native OS/CPU targets on Node 22.19 for candidate and staged-product npm checks, plus six Node 24 jobs including compiled standalone checks.

The general repository suite remains red. An earlier comparison found 105 failing test headers on the branch versus 107 on its master baseline, with no branch-only failures.

No production remote host, protocol, pairing, listener, or service is enabled. Signed/downloaded archive behavior, real off-LAN access, and production security/lifecycle acceptance remain unverified. No merge or release is authorized by this PR.

# feat: continue desktop work from Telegram and Discord by ashx-j · Pull Request #96 · ashx-j/lunR

Working away from the desktop needs more than a bot that forwards prompts. This adds guided gateway setup and phone controls, plus safe continuation of the same saved conversation between the TUI and Telegram or Discord.

*   Configure bots, a saved model, project roots, and login or boot startup. Service commands check native installation and daemon health.
*   Browse projects and saved sessions from owner-only private chats. Use native commands, chat approvals, file exchange, and background-result delivery.
*   Mark a TUI session with /handoff, pick it up with /continue, and reopen fresh state with /reclaim. Marks last eight hours and survive continuation.
*   Enforce one writer before mutable session loading. Preserve the selected branch, project directory, and permission checkpoint; refuse transfer while children or tracked processes remain active. SDK inspection can use SessionManager.openReadOnly; mutable managers must be disposed before reopening.

### Validation

*   398 tests pass across 30 gateway, session, and lifecycle suites.
*   All five offline package builds and the coding-agent Node bundle pass.
*   First-paint and first-turn subagent/MCP/LSP/fetch checks pass with the unchanged tool payload.
*   A compiled-gateway check with a local model verifies desktop continuation, original cwd, a real write-tool approval through chat, file download, and desktop reclaim.
*   Installer checks pass 28/29. The remaining expired pre-0.2.0 inference assertion also fails against unchanged master files.

Live Telegram/Discord interactions and native service installation/reboot behavior still need host verification. No release, global CLI update, or startup-service installation was performed. Project selection is a working directory, not a shell sandbox; all concurrent writers must use the updated session core.

Built with openai-codex/gpt-6-astra in lunR, with delegated session-ownership implementation.

# feat: include browser by default with a settings toggle by ashx-j · Pull Request #93 · ashx-j/lunR

The browser should work after installing lunR, without opting into another feature. It is now built in and on by default. Normal npm installation and updates install matching Chromium automatically, while Browser in `/settings` hides the tool and closes active or initializing contexts immediately.

Chromium installation runs only during installation or user-invoked setup/repair. Startup, ordinary builds, and model tool calls never download or launch it. Offline and `--ignore-scripts` installations keep the rest of lunR usable; missing binaries return `lunr browser install` recovery guidance. Existing matching caches are reused. Legacy explicit browser disable remains respected until the user changes the new setting.

The browser still uses isolated ephemeral sessions, accessible targets, bounded output/tabs, existing interaction permissions, and checked-IP routing. Search remains discovery and fetch remains URL reading. Private-network access is a separate explicit global setting.

### Validation

*   Five offline package builds and coding-agent Node bundle pass.
*   139 tests pass across nine focused suites, including actual Windows Chromium, settings persistence/legacy precedence, dynamic tool hiding/restoration, and active/pending cleanup.
*   A staged public-name npm fixture verifies automatic lifecycle execution, ignored scripts, offline/skip-download behavior, and failed-install recovery. The installer is present in the npm pack; shrinkwrap and standalone installer locks retain its lifecycle metadata.
*   Automatic installer and explicit CLI repair reuse the isolated matching Chromium cache. Local-provider CLI auto, Plan, and missing-browser flows pass.
*   Default-on and disabled first-request schema checks pass while browser runtime imports are stalled, along with existing first-use checks.
*   Changed-core/test Biome, lock checks, relative imports, and diff checks pass.

The network policy is defense in depth, not an OS sandbox. Private-network opt-in also lets public pages contact local services. Website effects cannot be undone. Linux/macOS browser launches and compiled Bun installation remain unvalidated. Headless fixture processes retain the existing forced-exit workaround. The prior broader run's gateway-inference failure was reproduced on unchanged master.

No merge, publication, global CLI update, or original-checkout build changes.

Implemented with OpenAI GPT-6 Astra in lunR.

Routine subagent updates were entering parent model context and encouraging extra coordination turns. Hiding the messages in the UI did not remove that cost.

This keeps new-protocol progress and inactivity diagnostics out of parent context, while actionable handoffs and blocking decisions still reach the parent. Communication cards collapse to clickable rows with readable sender/recipient descriptions. Legacy progress, failure delivery, cancellation protections, and terminal acknowledgements remain intact.

Also fixes a headless deadlock: waiting for child completion inside `agent_end` prevented queued decision requests from reaching the parent. The wait now yields to pending messages.

## Verification

*   296 focused tests pass across 16 suites.
*   Five offline package builds, Node bundle, touched-file lint, and diff checks pass.
*   Local scripted-provider CLI checks cover progress exclusion, handoffs, blocking replies, and parent questions.
*   First-paint and first-turn subagent/MCP/LSP/fetch checks pass with the updated tool-description fingerprint.

No measured token-savings claim. The separate existing cold-launch race before the first child status file remains outside scope. Installed CLI and computer-use worktrees are unchanged. Private transcripts, prompt snapshots, and local artifacts are excluded.

Implemented with `openai-codex/gpt-6-astra` in lunR, with read-only subagent review.

# fix: make copyable blocks quiet and clickable by ashx-j · Pull Request #99 · ashx-j/lunR

# fix: refresh expired xAI OAuth before /refresh live /models by ashx-j · Pull Request #4 · ashx-j/lunR

## Why

`/refresh` reported `Refreshed 7 providers; xai failed.` SuperGrok OAuth access tokens expire; chat refreshes them via `getAuth`, but the live-catalog path returned the stored token as-is. `GET https://api.x.ai/v1/models` then returned HTTP 403 (`The OAuth2 access token could not be validated.`).

The toast also counted all 7 `LIVE_LIST_PROVIDER_IDS` slots, including skipped providers.

## Change

*   `refreshCredentialFor` calls `getAuth` first (same lock + persist path as chat)
*   Failed token refresh stays a per-provider error
*   Toast only reports attempted providers and includes `error` (`xai failed (HTTP 403)`)

## Tests

`npx vitest --run test/model-refresh-merge.test.ts test/model-runtime-catalog-auth.test.ts` — 13 passed

# perf: cut first-request startup latency by half by ashx-j · Pull Request #65 · ashx-j/lunR

Merged

Merged

## Conversation

[![@ashx-j](https://avatars.githubusercontent.com/u/281260375?s=80&v=4)](/ashx-j)

PR [#50](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/50) cut first-request startup latency, but its lazy lifecycle handling and public package checks had regressions. That merge was reverted. This replacement keeps the startup improvement and repairs the failure paths found in the follow-up review.

*   Keep web, LSP, MCP, and subagent implementations lazy while registering their tools and required hooks before the first request.
*   Isolate web request and curator state per extension factory. Close partial or in-flight MCP work, serialize LSP shutdown, and wait for subagent launch registration without serializing foreground children.
*   Emit gateway and cron `session_shutdown` before disposal, including reset, resume, switching, and eviction paths.
*   Restore the public RPC entry through a bundle-first wrapper. Validate wildcard exports and recursively scan staged compiled files before publishing.
*   Keep PR [perf: accept terminal input in 130ms and harden runtime safety #41](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/41) terminal sanitization out of this branch.

## Measurements

Windows, Node 24.15.0, local provider, ten samples per cell. Baseline `b709d12` has instrumentation only. No remote model or reboot-cold filesystem measurement.

First request

Before median / p95

After median / p95

Fresh profile

1988.8 / 2026.4 ms

968.2 / 1007.0 ms

Repeated launch

2597.6 / 2628.6 ms

970.6 / 993.5 ms

Median improvement is 51.3% fresh and 62.6% repeated. The complete default tool payload remains identical. These are controlled measurements, not a latency guarantee. First-use MCP status varied from about 126 ms to 3.1 seconds. Details and reproduction commands are in `packages/coding-agent/docs/interactive-startup.md`.

*   Offline builds pass for TUI, AI, agent, coding-agent, and orchestrator.
*   Focused lifecycle and package tests pass 89/89.
*   The built-CLI checker passes stalled and failed runtime cases, blocked optional imports, and real first-turn subagent, MCP, LSP, and fetch calls.
*   All four public-package dry-run packs pass. Relative imports, shrinkwrap, installer lock, workflow policy, browser smoke, and diff checks pass.
*   Full coding-agent Vitest matches the current baseline at 2431 passed, 112 unrelated Windows and stale-fixture failures, and 47 skipped. TUI retains four Windows symlink failures. Repository Biome retains 20 existing findings.

No release, catalog regeneration, installed-CLI change, or PR [#41](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/41) terminal change is included.

# fix: eliminate disabled-watchdog cold-start scans by ashx-j · Pull Request #25 · ashx-j/lunR

## Summary

*   remove eager Git worktree fingerprinting from watchdog construction and session binding
*   gate repository signatures on the effective main-watchdog enablement state
*   lazily establish the repo-edit baseline at the first relevant `before_agent_start`
*   clear signature state across session and disable boundaries
*   add regression coverage for disabled startup, enabled change review, pre-existing dirty files, and session rebinding

## Root cause

`MainWatchdogRuntime` computed the complete repository change signature in its constructor, then twice more while binding the initial session. This happened even though the main watchdog is disabled by default. The signature invokes Git status and stats/hashes dirty paths, so Windows cold filesystem, Defender, and OneDrive state could turn deferred subagent attachment into a multi-second first-prompt delay.

The fix removes all constructor/session-bind scans. An enabled repo-edit watchdog now fingerprints once at turn start and once at agent end, preserving the existing rule that only edits made during that turn trigger review.

## Verification

*   focused Vitest regression set: 25/25 passed
*   required tsgo build sequence passed: tui, ai, agent, coding-agent, orchestrator
*   touched-file Biome passed; the vendored watchdog source remains excluded by repository configuration
*   dirty-worktree startup benchmark: prompt-ready 2.23s, deferred attach 265ms, `pi-subagents` factory 6ms

The full coding-agent suite was also attempted: 2236 tests passed and 125 failed in unrelated current-master/Windows areas; no watchdog test failed. Full Biome reports 35 existing errors and one warning outside the touched files.

## Out of scope

The larger first-paint ESM/TypeBox module graph remains a secondary cold-cache amplifier. This PR intentionally does not refactor that graph or the startup profiler; it fixes only the experimentally isolated default-off watchdog scan.

I ran no tests or builds.

I interpreted "filed by a Grok model" as an explicit model attribution in the PR body or comments, **not** a PR that merely mentions Grok. For example, [#62](https://github.com/ashx-j/lunR/pull/62) discusses a Grok schema failure; that does not establish who filed it. A missing slug is likewise an attribution gap, not evidence that Grok authored the PR.

I cannot honestly claim the table contains every Grok-filed or slugless PR.
